answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fabricated outputs. Creating a hundred identities no longer grants free influence: each must tie up capital, and detected fraud burns it. A glacier-slow withdrawal delay gives auditors time to challenge suspicious work; a lantern-style public ledger exposes repeated patterns, while the nadir is the attacker losing the full stake.
